title: Prospectivity journey & signal-weighting canvas for model procurement
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create a repeatable canvas that maps buyer prospectivity journeys to model supply signals and produces a signal-weighted score used by procurement and platform roadmap. This ticket covers interviews, signal inventory, weighting heuristics, a scoring prototype, and a recommended operational integration (alerts + dashboard). Goal: give PMs and GTM teams a defensible, reproducible way to prioritize model sourcing/fallback work based on customer segments and outage/risk scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: Interview notes from >=8 procurement/prospect GTM stakeholders uploaded to Confluence
Signal inventory (latency, availability, quant-compat, pricing, contract cadence) with provenance for 20+ models
Signal-weighted scoring prototype (spreadsheet) demonstrating rank stability under 3 simulated outage scenarios
Dashboard wireframe and alerting rules defined for Console and Sales ops
Hand-off doc for Ops/Platform with clear integration checklist and SLO mapping

decisions: Use a small set of normalized signals (latency, p95 variance, pricing volatility, quant-compatibility, contractual exposure, regional-coverage) to keep scoring tractable.
Weighting strategy will be segment-aware: pre-sales latency-first customers get higher latency weight; enterprise procurement gets higher contractual exposure weight.
Prototype scores will be presented as 0-1 normalized values and bucketed into: Green (>0.7), Amber (0.4-0.7), Red (<0.4).
tradeoffs: Simplicity vs fidelity: fewer signals make adoption easier but hide edge-case risks (e.g., kernel incompatibilities).
Automated weighting vs human override: automation speeds ops but requires guardrails to avoid blind substitutions.
Frequency of signal refresh: high cadence improves timeliness but increases noise and cost of data collection.
